system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}

CONCEPT: Knowledge Graph Management System

ATOM KGBDP-C10-S1-02 (S1): Bellomarini et al. define a knowledge graph as a semi-structured datamodel with three components: a ground extensional component (relational constructs for schema and data, modelable as graphs or generalizations), an intensional component (inference rules over the ground extensional constructs), and a derived extensional component produced by applying the rules to the ground component through reasoning.

EVIDENCE:
[KGBDP-p0035-s11] “A semi-structured datamodel characterized by three components: (i) a ground extensional component, that is, a set of relational constructs for schema and data (which can be effectively modeled as graphs or generalizations thereof); (ii) an intensional component, that is, a set of inference rules over the constructs of the ground extensional component; (iii) a derived extensional component that can be produced as the result of the application of the inference rules over the ground extensional component (with the so-called “reasoning” process).” – Bellomarini et al., 2019 – [40].

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — The three component definitions are independently assessable; separate them from the claim that the model has three components. / Joins the overall three-component definition with detailed definitions of each of the three components.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT: hold — Drop the attribution to Bellomarini et al.; assess the three-component definition itself. / Specific definition by one author group (Bellomarini et al., 2019); not a fixed consensus definition without the citation.
